title: Tenant migration windows and strict-semver routing for model/runtime pair stability
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers running pinned model versions experience silent failures or quality regressions when runtime and model versions are incompatible. We need tenant-aware migration windows and stricter semver-based routing rules to reduce incidents during runtime upgrades and model rollouts.

Goal: Implement a migration assistant that enforces compatibility rules, offers a tenant-level scheduled migration window, provides automated staged routing with rollback gates, and exposes clear telemetry for operator decisions. The feature should be opt-in per tenant and support both hosted and dedicated deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Admin UI: per-tenant migration schedule can be created and edited in Console
Routing: system enforces runtime->model compatibility matrix and blocks incompatible pairings unless explicit override is set
Canary policy: staged traffic rollout with configurable percentages (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) and automated health checks at each step
Rollback: automated rollback triggers on token_error_rate > 0.5% OR quality regressions from evaluation harness
Telemetry: a dashboard showing per-tenant model/runtime pairings, active migration windows, success/failure rates and last compatibility check
Backwards compatibility: existing pinned tenants remain pinned unless migrated via the assistant
technical_notes: Compatibility rules: adopt strict-semver for runtime (major.minor.patch). Compatibility only guaranteed when runtime_major == model_major and runtime_minor >= model_min_required_minor

Fallback policy: if runtime upgrade occurs and a pinned model is incompatible, route to last-compatible runtime variant in the same LTS channel; if none available, route to compatibility-fallback model (quantized or older checkpoint)

Implementation: central compatibility service will expose HTTP endpoints for routing decision with TTL-cached matrices. Local runtime agents will consult this service at route time with tenant id and model spec
Data migration: store per-tenant migration windows and overrides in the config DB; config DB schema migration planned in PR #8421
Performance: add cache layer to reduce p50 routing decision latency impact to <2ms for hot tenants
Trade-offs: stricter rules reduce risk but increase operational maintenance for customers who run mixed-version fleets. We will allow explicit tenant overrides with audit logging.
Security: sensitive operations (force-override) require SSO + audit log entry and MFA for enterprise tier accounts
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): feature flags + compatibility service in staging, unit/integration tests (now)
Phase 1 (canary tenants): enable assistant for 5 internal tenants and 2 pilot customers for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (beta): open to opt-in tenants via Console; restrict to hosted deployments first; monitor for 4 weeks
Phase 3 (GA): enable for all new tenants; provide migration tooling for existing pinned tenants and recommended schedules
Safety gates: require 0 critical errors and token_error_rate <= 0.25% for 7 consecutive days before progressing phases
Rollback plan: global kill-switch to disable routing enforcement which falls back to previous pin semantics; runbook: ENG-RR-003
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: compatibility-service outage could add latency or incorrectly block traffic. Mitigation: local agent fallback to cached last-known-matrix and last-compatible runtime; circuit-breaker with conservative allow-list for critical tenants
Risk: operator confusion from automatic migrations. Mitigation: readable audit trail, console notifications, and scheduled migration windows with email alerts
Risk: inaccurate compatibility rules leading to quality regressions. Mitigation: integrate regression checks using existing eval harness and hold rollouts behind evaluation pass
Risk: dedicated customers with air-gapped control planes may need different rollout mechanics. Mitigation: provide a schema export + offline compatibility checker for private deployments
